adequacy_predicate.description: Rung is adequate iff it certified a factor (gcd>1 or trial hit) or its trial bound covers sqrt(n). Certification is a function of n and the rung bound, not a model self-score.

dependencies_note: Catalog depends on WFA-0044 (IR spec) and WFA-0039 (stopping-rule extract). Neither artifact is on this worktree. This unit ships a hermetic IR-shaped L0-L3 ladder with source_anchor on every node, a measurable adequacy predicate, and an invocation bound. Disclosed, not hidden as a caveat on PASS. cloud ok=true is not delivery.

escalation_bound.agents_md_4b: two strikes on the same inadequacy fingerprint then pivot; a stuck scheduler that cannot pivot is stopped by the invocation bound

evidence.claim: An escalation trace per input showing which rung ran, why it escalated, and where it stopped.
Cost-versus-outcome against always running the top rung at equal labels; a ladder that escalates on every input is rejected as a more expensive top rung with extra steps.

question: An operator that runs the cheapest adequate source first and escalates to a more expensive one only when a typed adequacy predicate fails, with the predicate measurable and a bound on total escalations so the ladder cannot loop.

reviewer.note: Probe 2 re-runs the stuck never-adequate scheduler with and without the invocation bound and does not author progressive.py.

does_not_claim: WFA-0044 IR spec was present on this worktree
WFA-0001 schema pack was present on this worktree

tests.name: the escalation bound must be enforced and tested by an input that would otherwise loop
the adequacy predicate must be measurable, not a model self-assessment of its own output
cost and outcome must both be reported; a cheaper ladder with worse outcomes is not an improvement

title: Fusion operator: progressive, cheapest adequate source first, escalate only when a typed adequacy predicate fails
